chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade coming to the birds at night, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'The night is a security for them.'

key_terms.إِتْيَانِ: Coming to / approaching (in the context of hunting)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hunting birds at night and the reasoning behind it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the prohibition of night hunting for birds, grounding the ruling in the natural instinct for security (aman) that animals experience during darkness. In Shia jurisprudence, this reflects the principle of *ihsan* (benevolence) towards creation, ensuring that hunting does not exploit an animal's vulnerable state of rest. The narration highlights the Prophet’s (saww) attention to the physiological and behavioral needs of fauna, linking legal permissibility to ethical treatment.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, froom Sahl Bin Ziiyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from coming to the birds (for hunting) at night, and he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The night is a security for it’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah, from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Do not go to the baby birds in their nests at night or to the birds during their sleep [until the morning].’

A man then asked, ‘What is during their sleep, O Messenger of Allah?’ He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Night is their sleep, so do not enter in its sleep until the morning. Do not go to the baby birds in their nests until its feathers grow to fly. When it flies then aim your bow at it and fix for it your net.’”
